title: Founders of Routine share how they turned their products into a thriving global business.
description: Routine was selected as a 2019 SheEO Venture. The founders share their story and how this support is helping them build their business.

asr.full_text: The difference the sample price from the person who did the sample What was it like to send people to this sample space? How did you find the sample space? We had to be able to convince people to try natural deodorants and also while touching their armpits so it was not the sexiest endeavor, but people really caught on We had to get it into people's hands so sampling was actually a huge push of ours from the beginning we invested basically every single marketing dollar into sampling so that people could try it for themselves. The biggest hurdle I would say was the cash flow gap that we experienced. So initially we each put $250 into the company, and we bootstrapped our way and we hand piped every single jar ourselves. You know, worked out of basements and then moved into community kitchens and things like that. And then suddenly, demand got too big – we needed to focus on marketing and strategy, and we went to a facility. And…we suddenly were upfront paying for everything, and the cash flow gap got SO huge – we were just in a position – even though sales quadrupled that they were before – there was no money in the bank! So that was a huge hurdle that we had to overcome. We went actually through debt financing so we worked with the bank to secure a loan so that we could maintain the ownership of our company as that was really important to us. Yeah we didn't want to go with venture capital.

annotation.contextual_rationale: This video is non-scam content because it presents Routine co-founders discussing their natural-deodorant product, sampling approach, company growth, and a past business cash-flow problem. The bank loan discussion concerns maintaining ownership rather than asking viewers to invest, pay money, or provide private information, and the product sampling and event setting fit an ordinary business or commerce context.
annotation.fine_grained_rationale: Ordinary products and business operations are central: the founders discuss natural-deodorant sampling, product demand, startup cash flow and a bank loan used to maintain ownership of the company.
